scope: Full English chapters I-VII; To the Reader and Epistle to the Student; selected author errata and edition/contents mapping.

records.title: Three books have different purposes
records.source_statement: Book I introduces calculation, houses, planets, signs and technical terms; Book II handles horary questions; Book III handles nativities.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Seven prerequisites for learning
records.source_statement: Learn the ephemeris and chart erection, house topics, essential and accidental fortitudes, natural and accidental significators, signs, conditioned planetary descriptions and technical terms, especially chapters XX and XXI.
records.prerequisites: Apply these distinctions before judgement.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Competence prerequisites are not evidence that a judgement is correct.

records.title: Declared dependence is not a translation
records.source_statement: Lilly calls the introductory method his own, not a translation, while naming earlier authors with whose work he compared his notes.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This is author-reported provenance; individual dependencies must still be located.

records.title: Horary reconciliation is author intervention
records.source_statement: Lilly says he consulted named printed and manuscript authorities, reconciled disagreements, corrected translation problems and sometimes judges differently from the ancients.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not count Lilly and the authorities he reuses as automatically independent testimony.

records.title: Natal method includes stated disagreement with Ptolemy
records.source_statement: He names Leovitius as a major source of method and material for nativities, lists other sources, and acknowledges dissenting from Ptolemy in favour of reason and experience.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Preserve the disagreement instead of harmonizing the authors by default; experience is his claim, not an independently audited dataset.

records.title: Scope is not all astrology
records.source_statement: Lilly distinguishes the subjects treated here from elections, conjunctions, eclipses, comets and annual/monthly or weather material not fully methodized in this volume.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not infer complete coverage of those techniques from the title Christian Astrology.

records.title: Correct the author-listed errata before use
records.source_statement: The reader is asked to correct the errata before entering the discourse.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The errata list is PDF888; maintain original and corrected readings separately and do not apply uncertain page/line targets by guess.

records.title: Historical practice ethics
records.source_statement: The student is urged not to terrify the miserable with harsh judgement, not to let wealth procure a false judgement, and not to betray secrets.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The surrounding Christian, political and spiritual framing is retained as historical framing, not an empirical basis for calculation.

records.title: Classical planets and nodes
records.source_statement: Seven bodies are listed as planets: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury and Moon; the Dragon head and tail are expressly nodes, not planets.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This is the source taxonomy, not a modern astronomical classification.

records.title: Zodiac units and order
records.source_statement: There are twelve signs from Aries onward, each thirty degrees; a degree contains sixty minutes, and the circle contains 360 degrees.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Longitude example and sinister sextile
records.source_statement: Gemini 10 degrees is longitude70; adding60 degrees gives Leo10 at longitude130.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Five ordinary configurations
records.source_statement: Sextile, square, trine and opposition use60,90,120,180 degrees; conjunction is occupancy of the same degree and minute.
records.prerequisites: Exact configurations in this introductory description.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Later orb and application chapters must be retained; this definition alone does not supply an orb.

records.title: Qualities of ordinary aspects
records.source_statement: Sextile is moderately good; square is enmity and not good; trine denotes unity, concord and friendship; opposition is bad.
records.prerequisites: Use within the source enquiry, not as an unconditional modern personality classifier.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Conjunction depends on the question
records.source_statement: Conjunction is good or ill according to the nature of the question demanded.
records.prerequisites: The enquiry must be identified.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not assign one universal positive or negative value to all conjunctions.

records.title: Opposite signs
records.source_statement: Aries/Libra, Taurus/Scorpio, Gemini/Sagittarius, Cancer/Capricorn, Leo/Aquarius and Virgo/Pisces are opposite pairs.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Ephemeris reference epoch
records.source_statement: The ephemeris gives daily positions at noon, with other hours obtained by correction and equation.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: No modern civil timezone, calendar conversion or time scale is supplied by this introductory definition.

records.title: Latitude-specific teaching table
records.source_statement: The January1646 ephemeris and52-degree house table are supplied for teaching, with a stated adequacy claim for England on the indicated side of Newark upon Trent.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not use that historical local approximation as a universal latitude-independent house calculation.

records.title: Latitude-column letters
records.source_statement: M and S indicate meridional/south and septentrional/north latitude; A and D indicate ascending and descending latitude.
records.prerequisites: The letter must come from the latitude annotation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: D is not automatically direct motion.

records.title: Motion-column letters
records.source_statement: R identifies retrograde motion; Di or D identifies direct motion.
records.prerequisites: Read the motion column, not the latitude heading.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Solar ecliptic latitude
records.source_statement: The Sun has no latitude in this ecliptic reference system.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Dragon tail need not be separately tabulated
records.source_statement: The Dragon tail is in the sign and degree opposite the head even though not entered separately in the ephemeris.
records.prerequisites: Same node convention and epoch.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The chapter does not select a modern mean-node or true-node implementation.

records.title: Sign change at thirty degrees
records.source_statement: A planet that has passed thirty degrees proceeds in order into the next sign.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Read latitude separately from longitude
records.source_statement: The daily degree/minute entries and the lower latitude table have different meanings; use the heading to identify north/south and ascending/descending.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Aspect-table roles
records.source_statement: Six columns contain lunar aspects and their times, and the outer column contains mutual aspects of the other planets.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Solar-relative phase labels
records.source_statement: Occidental is explained as setting after the Sun and oriental as rising before it.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Preserve the local definition; no visibility threshold is added.

records.title: Noon-origin day
records.source_statement: The ephemeris day runs from noon to the next noon;14 hours after Tuesday noon means02:00 on Wednesday.
records.prerequisites: A dated local noon origin.
records.qualifications_and_limits: A clock conversion is not a Gregorian/Julian conversion or a civil-UTC conversion.

records.title: Zero and24 hours
records.source_statement: Zero after noon means noon; the next noon begins a new dated day rather than being called24 hours after the old noon.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Lunar phase sequence
records.source_statement: Conjunction with the Sun is the change/new Moon; the next square is first quarter, opposition full Moon, and the following square last quarter.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Printed lunar-distance labels
records.source_statement: This witness describes Apogaeon as nearest Earth and Perigaeon as most remote.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Image confirms the printed wording. This terminology is not silently corrected or used in astronomical computation; interpretation remains a witness issue.

records.title: Additional aspects are introduced for recognition
records.source_statement: The additional aspects listed are semisextile30, quintile72, tredecile108, biquintile144 and quincunx150 degrees; Lilly says he seldom uses more than the ordinary five and explains these for recognition.
records.prerequisites: Do not treat mere listing as equal operational endorsement.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Twelve house-table pages
records.source_statement: Each large page is headed by a solar sign; the relevant page is used to erect the figure.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This is a table-reading instruction, not the complete geometry of a house system.

records.title: Geometrical house membership
records.source_statement: The space from the first cusp to the second is the first house, and analogously for the other spaces.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Geometrical position must remain separate from the later assignment of virtue near a cusp.

records.title: Five-degree cusp virtue
records.source_statement: A planet within five degrees of a house cusp is assigned virtue to the house whose cusp is nearest, with a promise of further treatment.
records.prerequisites: Retain its geometrical house and the relevant cusp separately.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Exact five-degree equality, directional reach, overlaps, sign boundaries and later qualifications are not resolved by this one sentence.

records.title: Erection inputs
records.source_statement: Identify year, month, weekday, hour or fraction, the noon Sun position and the corresponding table time.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Solar-degree rounding restricted to horary
records.source_statement: For table entry, minutes exceeding30 select the next degree and minutes below30 the current degree; Lilly asserts no error for a horary question.
records.prerequisites: This is the local horary approximation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Exactly30 minutes is not specified, and natal accuracy must not inherit this tolerance.

records.title: Table-time addition and wrap
records.source_statement: Add the elapsed question time to the tabulated time corresponding to the Sun degree; subtract24 hours when needed and find the remaining or nearest table entry.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Tie handling and exact24-hour handling require a declared computation convention.

records.title: First erection example
records.source_statement: January6 at13:30 uses Capricorn26d39m rounded to27, table19h56m plus1h30m yielding21h26m and the six quoted cusps.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Opposite cusp completion
records.source_statement: Opposite houses receive opposite signs at the same degree and minute:10/4,11/5,12/6,1/7,2/8,3/9.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Intercepted signs
records.source_statement: A sign absent from the cusps but included between two house cusps is called intercepted; Aries in the worked chart is the example.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Placement relative to cusp degrees
records.source_statement: Place the planet within or before the relevant house according to its degree relative to the cusp and preserve a retrograde marker.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The explanatory placements use noon longitudes until corrected in the next chapter.

records.title: Noon chart is not yet event-time corrected
records.source_statement: Lilly explicitly says the planets in this erected chart have not yet been rectified to the hour and promises the correction procedure.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Lunar separation and application
records.source_statement: After placing the planets, inspect what the Moon last separated from and to what she next applies.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This observation must retain event timing and meridian convention; it is not an extra independent chart.

records.title: Second erection example
records.source_statement: January17 at23:20 combines20h42m and11h20m to make32h02m, reduces to8h02m and uses the nearby8h00m row.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Repeated and intercepted signs are allowed
records.source_statement: Two or nearly three signs in one house, or one sign on several cusps, are not by themselves mistakes.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Morning clock equivalence
records.source_statement: January26 at09:45 is equivalent to January25 at21h45m after noon.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The following example takes the Sun from January26 noon despite the previous-noon time origin; retain both printed choices rather than silently reconciling their epoch.

records.title: Third table-time example
records.source_statement: The printed third example adds21h18m and21h45m, reduces43h03m to19h03m and selects the nearby19h01m entry.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Solar position sanity check
records.source_statement: The four intervals noon/sunset/midnight/sunrise correspond respectively to house groups9-8-7,6-5-4,3-2-1 and12-11-10.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Event boundaries and local solar noon are not silently equated with civil clock hours.

records.title: Signed daily motion
records.source_statement: For direct motion subtract the earlier noon longitude from the later; for retrograde find the magnitude in the opposite direction and retain the reversal.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Full-circle wrap and sign changes require explicit unit handling.

records.title: Daily examples
records.source_statement: The examples give Saturn2m, Jupiter6m retrograde, Mars46m, Sun61m, Venus69m, Mercury87m, Moon12d07m and the head46m backwards.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Cross-sign lunar motion
records.source_statement: Capricorn20d54m to Aquarius3d01m gives12d07m of daily motion.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Existing OCR misread the prose3 as2; the original image agrees with the arithmetic. This is not a source contradiction.

records.title: Head motion may change direction
records.source_statement: The head sometimes moves forward and sometimes backward and should be observed in the ephemeris.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: No modern mean/true-node choice is explicitly named.

records.title: Different precision for questions and nativities
records.source_statement: Whole degrees may suffice for non-lunar horary placements in this teaching passage, but nativities require degrees/minutes and the Sun minutes/seconds because its motion sets annual revolutions.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not weaken the project verified ephemeris path or claim these historical tolerances validate approximation.

records.title: Hourly proportional table
records.source_statement: The hourly rate is the daily rate divided by24; units propagate from degrees/minutes/seconds/thirds to the next smaller sexagesimal units.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Solar and Martian hourly examples
records.source_statement: Daily61 arcminutes becomes2m32s30thirds per hour;46 arcminutes becomes1m55s.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Mercury sum and truncation
records.source_statement: For87 arcminutes, combine the60 and27 rows; the exact sum is3m37s30thirds, while Lilly drops the thirds and uses3m37s.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Lunar sum and truncation
records.source_statement: For12d07m daily, combine the12-degree and7-minute components to obtain30m17s30thirds per hour; the text permits discarding seconds/thirds in the lunar example.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Meridian offset for positions
records.source_statement: For the cited Eichstadius ephemeris, add50 minutes of time to the London elapsed time because the source meridian is east of London.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This is the author-specified source-to-London offset, not a universal offset or modern time zone.

records.title: Worked solar correction drops time and precision
records.source_statement: Although the total adjusted time is2h20m, the example uses two hours at2m32s and yields a5m04s increment, explicitly omitting the remaining20 minutes.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Exact proportional arithmetic with all given inputs differs; preserve both rather than replacing the printed result.

records.title: Worked lunar correction is rounded
records.source_statement: The example adds two hours of rounded30-arcminute motion to the Moon20d54m and reports21d54m.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Not the result of the full2h20m and12d07m/day linear calculation.

records.title: Routine shorthand is labelled as shorthand
records.source_statement: For many figures Lilly describes approximate six-hour increments of15 arcminutes for Sun/Venus/Mercury and about3 degrees plus minutes for the Moon, while allowing fuller multiplication/division.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not generalize to all planets, exact natal timing or actual modern astronomy.

records.title: Meridian offset has opposite sign for aspect times
records.source_statement: For a tabulated aspect at14h after source noon, subtract50 minutes to obtain13h10m after London noon.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The image reads50 in both statements; OCR30 in the explanatory sentence is an extraction error.

records.title: Four quadrants and house divisions
records.source_statement: The meridian and horizon supply four quadrants, each divided into three houses, beginning from the east.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The prose alone is not a complete mathematical derivation of the chosen house system.

records.title: Quadrant correspondences
records.source_statement: The four quadrants receive named directional, seasonal, age and temperament correspondences, with houses12/11/10,9/8/7,6/5/4 and3/2/1 respectively.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: House groups
records.source_statement: Angles are1,10,7,4; succedents11,2,8,5; cadents3,12,9,6, with the broad class hierarchy stated.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: Individual house ordering
records.source_statement: The explicit strength order is1,10,7,4,11,5,9,3,2,8,6,12.
records.prerequisites: The accompanying comparison assumes two planets equally dignified.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Retain alongside the broader class statement rather than forcing all succedents ahead of all cadents.

records.title: Strength means effectiveness in the assigned topic
records.source_statement: Greater house power means greater power to effect what the planet signifies.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Effectiveness does not by itself supply favourable quality, moral character or calibrated probability.

records.title: Principal significator from the relevant cusp
records.source_statement: The Ascendant ruler or the ruler of the sign on the house relevant to the question is the significator being discussed.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Do not replace a topic-specific significator by one generic dominant planet.

records.title: Relational co-significator
records.source_statement: A planet in aspect or conjunction with the principal significator participates more or less and may assist or disturb the desired outcome.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This relational use differs from the natural house co-significator labels in chapterVII.

records.title: House almuten and figure almuten differ
records.source_statement: A house almuten has most dignities in the sign on the relevant cusp; the figure almuten has most essential and accidental power in the entire figure.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: No numerical dignity weights or universal tie break are supplied here.

records.title: Node aliases
records.source_statement: The Dragon head and tail are also called Anabibazon and Catabibazon.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Verify typography when using historical aliases as identifiers; numeric node geometry remains separate.

records.title: Three coordinate quantities
records.source_statement: Longitude is measured from Aries along the sign order, latitude north/south of the ecliptic, and declination north/south of the equator.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: House topics are prerequisites, not decoration
records.source_statement: Knowing planets and signs without house judgement is compared to possessions with nowhere to put them; the house of the enquiry must be identified.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Historical source statement; no empirical validation inferred.

records.title: House 1: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: life; stature, colour, complexion, form and shape of querent or native; in eclipses, great conjunctions and annual Aries ingress: common people/general state of the kingdom.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 2: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: estate, wealth/poverty, movable goods, lending, gain and loss; law: querent assistants; duel: querent second; eclipse: wealth of people; ingress: ammunition, allies, support and magazines.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 3: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: siblings, cousins, kin, neighbours, small/inland journeys, removals, letters, rumours and messengers; none separately specified in this passage.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 4: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: fathers, land, houses, inheritance, tillage, hidden treasure, end of things, towns/cities/castles, gardens and nature of ground; sign represents town and its lord the governor in the relevant enquiry.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 5: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: children, pregnancy, childbirth enquiry, banquets, alehouses, taverns, plays, ambassadors and state agents; father wealth; health of querent child; ammunition of a besieged town.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 6: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: servants, galley slaves, small cattle, illness nature/cause/duration/curability, labourers and agricultural occupations; father siblings; none separately specified in this passage.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 7: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: marriage, love, partner description, public enemies, defendant, opposing army, quarrels/duels, artist/astrologer, physician, theft, thieves and fugitives; annual ingress: war/peace and victory.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 8: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: estates of deceased, death quality, wills, legacies, dowry/portion and recovery, fear/anguish, heir; duels: adversary second; law: defendant friends.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 9: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: long or overseas journeys, clergy/religion, dreams/visions, foreign countries, books, learning, church livings and spouse kin; none separately specified in this passage.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 10: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: kings, rulers, judges, officers, commanders, mother, honour, preferment, dignity, office and trade/profession; kingdoms, empires, duchies and counties; London mayor example occurs under11.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 11: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: friends, friendship, hope, trust, confidence, praise/blame and fidelity; ruler favourites/counsellors/allies/treasure/ammunition/soldiery; republican council; London common council.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House 12: source-specific topics and correspondences
records.source_statement: private enemies, historical witchcraft allegations, great cattle, sorrow, imprisonment, self-undoing and secret malice; none separately specified in this passage.
records.prerequisites: Identify the enquiry and its house role before interpretation.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Body, colour, gender and social classifications are preserved as historical claims, not modern medical/demographic conclusions.

records.title: House natural co-significators are not cusp rulers
records.source_statement: The passage assigns signs and planets as natural co-significators of houses, and also names planetary joys.
records.prerequisites: Read these separately from the cusp ruler definition in chapterVI.
records.qualifications_and_limits: These roles can name different planets; no replacement of the actual cusp ruler is licensed.

records.title: Marks on face: conditions and author claim
records.source_statement: Saturn or Mars in the first is connected with a blemish; placement on the body follows the ascending sign, with upper/middle/lower subdivisions for the head example. Lilly claims hundreds of examples.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: The claimed examples are not furnished as an auditable validation dataset; no numeric boundaries for early/middle/late are supplied.

records.title: London is an explicitly contextual house example
records.source_statement: For London, the10th is the Lord Mayor, the11th the Common Council, and the Ascendant the commoners.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This historical example is not a generic mapping for any modern administrative system.

records.title: Concluding Ptolemaic attribution is a claim
records.source_statement: Lilly attributes his house account to Ptolemaic doctrine and his experience, and says he did not find verity in other Arabian divisions.
records.prerequisites: Within the specified source chapter and enquiry.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Attribution and personal assessment are preserved; agreement with the already extracted Ptolemy rules has not been established by that sentence.

records.title: Saturn first-house branch is not unconditionally adverse
records.source_statement: Moderately fortified Saturn in the first with the specified benevolent aspect is associated with a sober constitution and usually long life.
records.prerequisites: Fortification and benevolent aspect are both required.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Keep distinct from the first-house mark claim and do not issue health or longevity advice.

records.title: Mars third-house qualification
records.source_statement: Mars in the third is not very unfortunate unless joined with Saturn.
records.prerequisites: Third-house enquiry and the Saturn qualification.
records.qualifications_and_limits: Reduced unfavourableness is not automatically a fully favourable prediction.

records.title: Physician combination is local to sixth house
records.source_statement: The source associates Mars and Venus conjoined in the sixth house with a good physician.
records.prerequisites: Both named planets, conjunction and sixth-house placement.
records.qualifications_and_limits: This is not a diagnosis, treatment recommendation, or a universal talent inference.
